_comment: Meta MTIA v2 (2024) single-chip HAT twin. RB-05 nested: backing LPDDR5 DRAM -> on-chip shared SRAM -> per-PE local mem -> compute leaf (8x8 PE grid). NOTE: backing tier is LPDDR5 (NOT HBM) - 128 GB @ 204.8 GB/s, ~16x lower BW than an H100 HBM3 stack at comparable/higher capacity, deliberate for capacity-bound DLRM/recommendation inference. Field named 'hbm_bandwidth_bps' etc. retained for experiment-schema compatibility; mem_standard records actual LPDDR5. Sources: Meta AI blog, Hot Chips 2024, MTIA ISCA'25 paper, ServeTheHome/DCD.
arch_note: Standard backing-DRAM accelerator layout but backing tier is LPDDR5, not HBM: 128 GB @ 204.8 GB/s (16 channels x 16-bit x 6400 MT/s). Bandwidth is ~16x lower than an H100 HBM3 stack while capacity is comparable/higher - deliberate for capacity-bound recommendation inference rather than BW-bound training. Large 256 MB on-chip SRAM (2.7 TB/s) is the primary reuse buffer; 384 KB local memory per PE (1 TB/s) sits closest to compute. Single-chip twin; the production accelerator module packs 2 chips at 220 W.

provenance.source: Meta AI blog (next-gen MTIA); Hot Chips 2024; ServeTheHome MTIA2 teardown (LPDDR5 128 GB @ 204.8 GB/s). Energy + line_bytes are BRONZE LPDDR5 JEDEC estimates (unpublished).
Meta AI blog; MTIA ISCA'25 (256 MB shared on-chip SRAM @ 2.7 TB/s, 3.5x MTIA v1); ServeTheHome. (ServeTheHome '256 GB' is a typo.)
Hot Chips 2024; ServeTheHome (384 KB local memory per PE, 1 TB/s). BW per-PE vs aggregate slightly ambiguous -> SILVER.

Meta AI blog (177 TFLOPS dense BF16, 64 PE = 8x8 grid, 1.35 GHz); MTIA ISCA'25 (2.76 TFLOPS/PE = 1.383e12 MAC/s; Dot-Product Engine = 32x32 MAC tiles, output-stationary, BF16 in / FP32 acc). Device peak = 64 x 1.383e12 x 2 = 1.77e14 FLOP/s (177 TFLOPS). matrix_unit SILVER (cross-validated, not vendor-stated); energy_pj_per_mac BRONZE estimate.
